newsitem.title: USA: Everett, Wash. Water & Sewer Revs AA-minus -- S&P.
newsitem.headline: Everett, Wash. Water & Sewer Revs AA-minus -- S&P.

text.p: Standard & Poor's Corp on Thursday assigned its double-A'-minus rating to the City of Everett, Wash.'s water and sewer revenue bonds series 1997. The outlook is stable.

The outlook reflects Standard & Poor's expectation that the city's financial position will remain solid as future capital projects are undertaken. A stable local economy and ample water supply and treatment capacity also provide credit strength, Standard & Poor's said.
The rating on the city's bonds reflects the following credit strengths:
-- A stable local economic base (Snohomish County is rated double-A'- minus), with easy access to the broader Seattle metropolitan area;
Credit concerns include the presence of the Boeing Company as the area's largest employer (30,000 employees).

Located just north of Seattle, Everett (population 81,810) is Washington's fifth-largest city. The local economy is benefitting from the region's strong growth and continued diversification away from aircraft manufacturing and forestry-related industries.

While Boeing still remains the dominant employer in the area, a recently completed $1.5 billion expansion to the Everett facility should keep operations stable. The Navy Homeport recently went into operation and is expected to bring an additional 10,000 military and civilian personnel to the area.
Everett's wealth and income indicators are average, and unemployment, 7.3% in 1996, remains slightly higher than the county, state and U.S. averages.
The water system serves Everett as well as 40 water districts and 65 water purveyors and encompasses about 85% of Snohomish County.

The city's water source is the Sultan River, which provides a plentiful supply of raw water. Everett is also in the process of acquiring an additional 36mgd of water, previously owned by Weyerhauser Corp.

The water treatment facility, at 120mgd, has ample treatment capacity. The sewer system provides sanitary and storm service to Everett and three other water districts. The treatment facility (33mgd capacity) provides secondary treatment, and is expected to meet flows through 2010. Boeing, the largest retail customer, accounts for less than 3% of both water and sewer revenues.

Everett's rates remain competitive, with a combined bill at $42.15/1,000 cf. No rate increases are projected. The five-year capital program is a manageable $67 million, and will be primarily funded on a pay as you go basis.

Debt service coverage has been over two times since 1992. Projected combined coverage on all outstanding obligations, including transfers, is at least 1.50 times through 2002. The system has a strong liquid position, with about nine months' operating expenses on hand in fiscal 1996.
